history.dynasty: Queen Dhankaur of the Landaura Estate (Gurjar dynasty); renovated 1962-1963 by the Mahanirvani Akhada
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV lists Haridwar; the temple is actually in Kankhal, about 4 km south of Haridwar city - town corrected to Kankhal. Daksheshwar Mahadev (Daksha Mahadev) is the famous Shiva temple named after King Daksha Prajapati, father of Sati. It stands on the site where Daksha performed his great yagna (Brihaspatisava/Ashvamedha per the Shiva Purana, Mahabharata and Vayu Purana), deliberately not inviting Shiva; insulted by her father's treatment of her husband, Sati immolated herself in the sacrificial fire. Virabhadra, born of Shiva's anger, slew Daksha, who was later revived with a goat's head. The present temple was built by Queen Dhankaur in 1810 and rebuilt in 1962 (updated 1963 by the Mahanirvani Akhada). The complex holds the ancient yagna kund pit, Sati Kund, a Das Mahavidya temple (a Navratri Devi gathering place) and a Ganga temple, all in white-painted Nagara style with a tall central spire; the adjacent Daksha Ghat lies on the Neel Dhara canal of the Ganga. It is one of the five sacred places of Haridwar and a major Shaivaite Maha Shivaratri pilgrimage. Coordinates are the published Wikipedia coordinates, since the geocoder matched a different nearby shrine (Alankeshwar Mahadev).

name: Daksha Mahadev Temple
town_description: Kankhal, adjoining Haridwar to the south (about 4 km away), is an ancient heritage pilgrimage township now under a common municipal administration with Haridwar and Jwalapur since 1868. It is best known for the Daksheshwar Mahadev Temple on the site of King Daksha's legendary yagna, along with Sati Kund, the Ramakrishna Mission Sevashrama and the Anandamayi Ma Samadhi Mandir. The Daksha Ghat on the Ganga (Neel Dhara canal) is a quieter alternative to Har Ki Pauri for ritual bathing.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 38 km; taxis available).
travel.railway: Haridwar Junction (approx. 3.5-4 km; autos, shared autos and taxis to Kankhal).
travel.road: Easily reached by road from Haridwar city via bus, auto-rickshaw or taxi; roads are good and private vehicles can be used.

visitor_information.best_time: November to March; Maha Shivaratri and the Shravan month (when Shiva is believed to reside in Kankhal) are the most significant periods.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Commonly 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily (some sources say 6:00 AM-7:00 PM; one source lists 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 2:00-9:00 PM - verify). Free entry; holy dip at Daksha Ghat is a customary add-on.
